podcast.body: By her fourth album, *Wave*, released in 1979, Patti Smith exhibited a notable shift towards a smoother, more melodic sound. Produced by pop artist Todd Rundgren, the album, while still retaining anger and grit, presented these qualities beneath a "shiny, glossy" exterior, with Smith sounding calmer and less confrontational. It reached number 18 on the Billboard album chart. "By the time we get to her fourth album, Wave, there is this notable shift in her sound. In 1975, Patty Smith kind of kicked down the door of Rock and Roll with this album that sounded like poetry that was set on fire."

podcast.body: Produced by Todd Rundgren, *Wave* was Patty Smith's highest-charting LP on Billboard, peaking at number 18 on the album chart. Its most famous single, "Dancing Barefoot," became her most covered song after "Because the Night." "Patty Smith finished the 70s with her WAVE album produced by Todd Rungren."
